McLean County sits in central North Dakota. Washburn is the county seat. The county was founded before North Dakota became a state. It has a rural feel, lake access, farm land, small towns, and county held properties that may reach public sale after tax foreclosure. This guide explains how McLean County tax deed sales work, what bidders should check, and where to get updates.

What Are McLean County Tax Deed Sales?

McLean County does not sell private tax lien certificates. North Dakota stopped the sale of delinquent taxes to private lien holders. Instead, counties may sell land the county has already taken by tax deed after the legal tax foreclosure process. That makes this a tax deed style sale, not a classic tax lien certificate auction.

Important Details

Key Takeaways

  • McLean County sits in central North Dakota and holds tax deed sales for properties after tax foreclosure.
  • The annual tax deed sale occurs on the third Tuesday in November at 10:00 a.m. in the County Commission Chambers.
  • Investors can benefit from low-risk opportunities by buying parcels below market value, but due diligence is essential.
  • Bidders must check properties, confirm access, and be qualified to participate in the auction without owing delinquent taxes.
  • McLean County offers a favorable market for real estate investors with strong community ties and varied economic opportunities.

North Dakota law says the annual sale starts on the third Tuesday in November. McLean County sale notices have used 10:00 a.m. at the County Commission Chambers in the McLean County Courthouse. The county contact page lists the Auditor email as baknutson@nd.gov.

Fun Facts About McLean County

  • McLean County has about 9,740 residents by the latest Census estimate.
  • Washburn is the county seat. Garrison is a key lake area town.
  • Fort Stevenson State Park sits by Lake Sakakawea near Garrison.
  • Knife River Indian Villages was a major trade center on the Upper Missouri.

Attractions and Economic Highlights

  • Attractions: Fort Stevenson State Park, Lake Sakakawea, county museums, and nearby historic sites.
  • Transportation: U.S. Highway 83 and state roads connect Washburn, Garrison, Wilton, and Underwood.
  • Economy: agriculture, energy, public services, tourism, and lake based recreation.
  • Community: fishing, boating, hunting, small town events, and quiet rural living.

The county has high home ownership and a rural housing base. Census data shows 5,862 housing units and an owner occupied rate above 80 percent.

Why Is McLean County Good for Tax Deed Investors?

  • McLean County offers state tax lien opportunities in tax deed form.
  • Buyers bid on real property, not just a paper lien.
  • Minimum bids may be tied to taxes, costs, and county review.
  • Rural parcels may offer high returns when bought below true market value.
  • It can be a low risk investment only after strong research.
  • The best deals often need patient buyers with cash ready.

Auction Process for McLean County Tax Deed Sales

McLean County tax deed sales are public auctions. The county offers each parcel on its own. Bidding starts at or above the minimum sale price. The highest qualified bidder wins. McLean County notices say payment must be made in cash. The sale continues until all county forfeited parcels have been offered.

There is no starting interest rate to bid down. That matters. This is not a North Dakota tax lien auction where investors compete by lower interest. It is a county tax deed sale procedure. The return comes from the real estate deal, not from monthly lien interest.

How the Auction Works

  1. Review the list:

    Read the parcel number, legal description, taxes owed, and minimum sale price.

  2. Check the property:

    Confirm access, land use rules, utilities, flood risk, and condition.

  3. onfirm bidder rules:

    Ask the Auditor if any sign in is needed before 10:00 a.m.

  4. Bid at the sale:

    Each parcel is offered alone to qualified bidders.

  5. Pay as required:

    McLean County notices state cash payment.

  6. Record and plan:

    After county deed steps, handle title, insurance, cleanup, and resale.

North Dakota law says each parcel must sell to the highest qualified bidder for at least the minimum sale price. A person who owes delinquent taxes to any county is not qualified as the high bidder.

Maximum Returns and Expected Returns on McLean County Tax Deed Property

McLean County does not offer tax lien certificates with a fixed interest return. So there is no certificate yield to collect. Expected returns depend on purchase price, repair cost, title work, demand, access, and resale value.

The largest gains may come from buying a parcel far below its true market value. The risk is also real. Some parcels may be vacant, landlocked, damaged, occupied, or hard to insure. A smart buyer sets a max bid before the sale.

Open to All Investors and Foreign Investor Participation

I found no McLean County rule that limits bidders to local residents. North Dakota law focuses on bidder qualification, not local residency. The main rule is that the winning bidder must be qualified and must not owe delinquent taxes to any county.

Foreign investor participation may be allowed. Still, investors outside the U.S. should confirm payment rules, deed recording, tax forms, banking, and title insurance before the auction. Ask the Auditor and a North Dakota title expert before you bid.

Importance of Due Diligence in McLean County Tax Deed Investing

What Due Diligence Entails

  • Check the county parcel map and property value tools.
  • Read the legal description.
  • Visit the property if you can.
  • Run a title search.
  • Check special assessments.
  • Confirm roads and access.
  • Review city and township rules.
  • Estimate cleanup, taxes, and resale costs.

Risks of Skipping Due Diligence

  • You may buy land with no legal access.
  • A structure may need major repair.
  • Old liens or easements may affect use.
  • Special assessments may remain.
  • An occupied property may need legal steps.
  • A cheap parcel can become costly fast.

Buying Over the Counter Property in McLean County

How to Purchase Over the Counter Deeds

North Dakota law allows property not sold at the annual November sale to be sold by private sale before the next annual sale. It must be sold for at least the required minimum price unless the county follows a later reappraisal process. Ask the McLean County Auditor if any county held parcels are still available.

Benefits of Over the Counter Purchases

Over the counter deeds can reduce bidding stress. You may have more time to study the parcel. You may also avoid auction day pressure. The tradeoff is simple. Good parcels may already be gone. Always confirm the current price and title status.

Why McLean County Is a Top Choice for Tax Deed Investors

Economic and Tax Advantages

  • McLean County has a rural tax base and small town markets.
  • Energy, agriculture, tourism, and public jobs support demand.
  • The lake area adds appeal for recreation land.
  • The county location gives access to central North Dakota routes.
  • County tax deed sales can create property investment chances at public auction.

Real Estate Market Overview

McLean County has a small population and many housing units for its size. That can help buyers find homes, lots, farm related land, and rural tracts. Demand may vary by town. Lake area parcels may draw more interest. Remote land needs extra care.

Conclusion

McLean County tax deed sales can be useful for investors who want real property instead of tax lien certificates. The sale is usually tied to the third Tuesday in November. McLean County notices show a 10:00 a.m. Central Time start at the Courthouse Commission Chambers. The sale is cash based in county notices.

Do not bid from the list alone. Read every parcel. Check access. Check title. Check value. Then set your bid limit. In tax deed investing, the win is not just buying cheap. The win is buying a property you understand.

Pro Tips

  • Call the Auditor before travel. Confirm the list, payment, and sale room.
  • Watch rural township parcels near Lake Sakakawea with care. Access matters.
  • Study city lots in Garrison, Underwood, Washburn, Wilton, and Turtle Lake.
  • Budget for quiet title work if you plan to resell with clean title.
  • Do not chase every parcel. One clean deal beats five problem deals.

FAQs About McLean County Tax Deeds

Can I finance a tax deed purchase after the auction?

Most buyers should plan on cash first. Financing may come later.

Do I need quiet title after buying?

Often yes, if you want easier resale or title insurance.

Can I enter an occupied property right away?

No. Use proper legal steps before entry.

Are old mortgages wiped out?

Many interests may be cut off, but check title first.

Can I resell fast?

Maybe. Title, condition, and buyer demand decide that.
